case.question: What staffing and operating setup should we start with in each city: Dubai and Abu Dhabi?

answer.headline: Start with a small cross-trained kitchen + counter team in each city, led by one trained food-safety supervisor per site; align roles to mandatory food-handler training in both emirates and to the delivery channel you choose.

items.text: Proposal: launch each city as one compact production kitchen plus counter/pickup point sized for pizza-and-kebab prep, with delivery as a major channel from day one. Curated evidence shows a platform option where the platform supplies riders (Deliveroo Marketplace+) alongside your own delivery staff, with a selectable area and minimum spend; this affects whether you staff in-house riders.

Inference: pizza and kebab lines share ovens, flat-tops, and cold prep, so a single prep/cook team can cover both instead of separate pizza and grill brigades at launch; verify against your actual equipment layout and expected order mix.

sections.title: Staffing scenario per site (not a verified requirement)

items.text: Assumption: no branch format, audience, or budget was set in the profile, so the following counts are illustrative scenarios only, not verified requirements. Scenario for one compact site: 1 site manager/supervisor (also the trained food-safety lead), 2-3 kitchen staff cross-trained across dough/pizza and kebab/sandwich lines, 1-2 counter/cashier and packing staff per shift, 1 dishwasher/cleaner, plus 1 part-time in-house rider if you self-deliver rather than using platform riders.

Proposal: stagger shifts so a small core covers prep before opening, peak evening delivery, and a shorter late window; do not extend hours purely to match observed late-night competitors, since advertised competitor hours are branch-specific observations and not evidence that late-night staffing would be profitable.

Dubai: Dubai Municipality guidance requires food handling staff, supervisors, and managers to receive formal food safety training appropriate to their work activity, so budget training time for every kitchen and supervisor role before opening; the source is a 2023 version still linked as of 2026-10-12 and flagged for review, so confirm activity-specific applicability with the municipality.

Abu Dhabi: ADAFSA describes an Essential Food Safety Training programme for food handlers covering cross-contamination, cooking/processing, cleaning, chilling, and food safety management; the summary does not establish prices, wages, or staffing ratios, so treat all training-cost and headcount numbers as quotes to be obtained.

Dubai (and a proposal for Abu Dhabi pending local confirmation): Dubai Municipality transport guidance specifies hot food held at 60 C or above, cold at 5 C or below, frozen at -18 C or below, and requires sealed containers plus separation of hot and cold items into insulated secondary units. Build these checks into packing-station SOPs and staff training.

Proposal: if you run in-house delivery, add a rider-dispatcher or supervisor duty per shift for bag temperature checks, handover logging, and radius management; test a limited radius first and expand only after observing packing times and complaint rates. Neither the platform product page nor anecdotal competitor listings establish demand, so treat radius as a test variable.

sections.title: Kitchen roles, training and quality checks

items.text: Proposal: define four role cards at launch - dough/pizza, grill/kebab and sandwich assembly, packing and dispatch, and counter/order handling - each with a daily opening and closing check, a portion standard for the meaty pizza and kebab items, and a 60 C / 5 C / -18 C temperature log where applicable. Two pressured competitors in Dubai and Abu Dhabi list multiple pizza branches and Middle Eastern street-food formats, so consistent output is the differentiation lever.

Inference: with a Jordanian meaty-pizza and kebab-sandwich concept, retaining one Jordan-trained lead cook per site for the first months reduces recipe drift while local hires are trained; this is a reasoned interpretation, not a verified labour-market claim.

Curated evidence for this question returned no records on UAE staff wages, staff-to-volume ratios, licensing timelines, or supplier terms, and one operations source is flagged needs_review. Any headcount or cost schedule below should therefore be treated as a planning assumption until quotes and official confirmations are obtained.

assumptions: Business profile: Jordanian origin, core products meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches, target cities Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Branch format, startup budget, monthly rent budget, target audience, and positioning are unset, so all site-scale assumptions are placeholders.
All headcount numbers per site are illustrative scenarios, not verified staffing requirements.
No UAE wage, rent, or commission figures were supplied or verified, so no cost model is presented.
next_steps: Inspect the Dubai Municipality training guidance and delivery-vehicle guidance pages directly to confirm which roles and temperature rules apply to your setup, then build training and temperature-log SOPs.
Confirm ADAFSA Essential Food Safety Training deadlines and any premises-specific requirements for an Abu Dhabi site before finalising the Abu Dhabi roster.
Draft a one-page role card for each launch position and run a 30-day roster test in one city before replicating it in the second.

If you want a break-even view, collect these eight inputs: average order revenue, food cost per order, packaging cost per order, other variable cost per order, delivery share of orders, delivery commission rate, monthly fixed costs, and operating days per month.
questions: What site size and channel mix do you plan for each city (for example dine-in/counter plus delivery, or delivery-only kitchen), and how many covers or orders per day are you designing for?

If you want me to calculate contribution and break-even, what are your average order revenue, food cost per order, packaging cost per order, other variable cost per order, delivery share, commission rate, monthly fixed costs, and operating days per month?
